correctness.rationale: The simultaneous action scores are exactly C_i(b)=p_i+1_{i=b} and rebel costs R_i(a)=q_i+1_{i=a}, for all m and nonnegative integer pinned counts. If Q has two members contained in P, every best-responding rebel must choose b in Q and the conformist must copy b, after which the rebel strictly prefers another Q member. In the complement Q\P nonempty, choose a in P, b in Q\P; integrality makes the at-most-one matching bonus harmless. If Q singleton in P, a=b its member is a simultaneous response. The constructions include all ties and m=2 boundary. The independent enumeration directly searched all m=2,3 triples of counts and m=4 binary-valued counts (1,066 profiles), with 118 obstructed, comparing full pure response matrices; this finite test corroborates, rather than proves, the universal argument.

value.rationale: A sharp, constructive local equilibrium/nonexistence criterion for an identifiable subgraph of a natural multi-strategy conformist–rebel game, extending the uniform pinned motif to arbitrary asymmetric integer counts. A concrete three-strategy nonuniform obstruction lies outside the earlier degree/strategy existence regime. This is more than a restatement of matching pennies, though not a global characterization for arbitrary interacting flexible vertices.

final_claim: For a conformist–rebel adjacent pair all of whose other neighbors are stubborn, and m>=2 pure strategies, no simultaneous pure best-response pair exists precisely when the rebel pinned-count minimizer set Q has at least two elements and lies inside the conformist pinned-count maximizer set P. This is a sufficient whole-network obstruction, and a necessary/sufficient criterion for a network with just these two flexible agents.
limitations: No complete global equilibrium classification for networks with many flexible agents
No mixed equilibrium or dynamic convergence claim
Finite test covers only 1066 count-vector profiles
